subject: crowbar
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: crowbar, in the place of the game's models/v_crowbar.mdl, models/p_crowbar.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_shotgun.mdl, models/w_9mmar.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, D, A, B where the asset was D, B, C, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Views show a long straight bar with a hooked claw at one end (top, below, front-left) and a flattened wedge at the other (left, right, front-right). That is a crowbar's outline, as the brief asks. The top view shows a slight bow in the shaft, which reads as a bent tool rather than a missing or extra part.

M2.reason: Measured length 31.8 against the brief's 32 (0.7% off), well inside 15%. The 2 and 7.2 width and thickness are not set by the brief.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies, down to the small ones: (1) red-painted shaft, present; (2) curved claw at one end with a pointed tip, present in left, top, below and in-hand; (3) flat wedge end at the other, present in left, right and front-right; (4) bare-metal tips on both ends, present as grey. No part is missing, and the brief names no rivets, teeth or facets. The shaft's facet count is not in the brief, so it cannot be charged.

M4.reason: Shaft is red paint with darker shading, as the brief asks. Both tips are grey steel, matching the game's own crowbar colour in first-person.png and the lineup. No region is in the wrong colour or material.

M5.reason: The brief asks for worn tips, and they are there as bare metal at both ends. No markings are asked for, and none are missing; the shaft's darker bands are lighting on a plain painted bar, not a fault. Nothing extra is added.

M6.reason: Scored 2 as the brief for this judging directs, with the line-up measured apart. The line-up record shows the asset picked as the odd one out in 2 of 4 readings (picks D, D, A, B against assets D, B, C, B). The rubric's cap for picked twice or more is 1, and the record's own summary ('passed') disagrees with its counts. The cap is applied from the measurement, not by this score.

M7.reason: The w_ model lies flat along its length as a crowbar would rest on the ground, with the claw and blade at either end. The brief names no front, and no fault is visible in the views. Its origin looks like a bar's centre, not a floating or tilted pose.

M8.reason: SMAK check returns no errors. 60 triangles is far under twice the median of Half-Life's weapons (142) and under the third quartile (187). The views show no gaps, inverted faces or floating parts: the claw and shaft join in front-left, back-left and below, and the flat end is closed.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset's claw sits where the game's own crowbar sits, at the same angle and the same way round, with the shaft running down out of frame. In attack.png the weapon stays in the hand through the swing: frames 1 and 2 have it carried out of the picture, which does not count as leaving the hands, and frame 3 shows the grip at the bottom of the picture.
